doc.title: JJ Johnson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Jazz at the Philharmonic and Count Basie
title: Reaction to his first solo with Basie
summary: Reviewers doubted anyone could play so fast on slide trombone; Johnson says he was puzzled by the fuss.

story.theme_name: Trombonists: who they heard, admired and learned from
story.community_name: Talking trombonists: who played the slide and how

blocks.x: Jay, can you recall the reaction to that first solo with him? What was it? The King? I can’t remember if that was it.
It may have been The King.

But I can remember reading the reviews. There were all kinds of arguments on the part of Leonard Feather and others. They said, " Nobody can play that fast on the trombone. It must be a valve trombone."
[I was] just wondering what your reaction was because it was in Metronome [magazine] and Down Beat [magazine], and it was [as] though somebody had – people went ballistic . . .
. . . because this was the first time they had heard you in a setting that was an international kind of band.

Uh huh. I don’t remember what my feelings or reactions were about the reviews and about the commentary. I just don’t have any recollection. If anything, I might have been puzzled by it all because I didn’t think it was a big deal. I wasn’t trying
to set the world on fire. [laughter] I was just trying to do what I was hired to do, and it came out well and that’s all I can say about it.
